Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

baseballscouting 0.1.0

Simulation (at_bat_sim())

  • Outcome probabilities now depend on the batter, the pitcher, and the sampled pitch type and location. Previously every matchup drew from the same fixed league distribution, and a batter with no data in the sampled location bin always struck out.
  • Batter and pitcher per-PA outcome rates are shrunk toward league rates and combined with the odds-ratio (generalized log5) method. Hit outcomes are then scaled by the batter’s smoothed hit rate on the sampled pitch type and location.
  • Rates are per plate appearance (the old code divided by pitches).
  • The default league baseline is normalized to sum to 1 (it summed to 0.985).
  • Results are no longer fixed by a hard-coded set.seed(42). With seed, results are reproducible and identical for any num_cores.
  • The function returns the data frame instead of printing it. The returned data frame lists all eight outcomes in a fixed order and carries a "matchup" attribute with the inputs.
  • New optional arguments: seed, league_rates, prior_pa, location_prior_pa, multiplier_range, game_types, verbose.
  • Data now comes from the same Baseball Savant request as the report functions. baseballr::statcast_search_*() (baseballr 1.6.0) fails against the current Savant CSV, so baseballr is no longer a dependency.
  • Warns when either player has fewer than 50 PAs in the window.

Reports (generate_pitcher(), generate_hitter())

  • Dates control the data range. A hard-coded 2024 season filter is removed.
  • Spring training is excluded by default. New optional game_types argument.
  • The pitcher strike-zone heat map orientation is fixed: zone 1 is top-left, from the catcher’s view.
  • Whiff rate is whiffs per swing, matching Baseball Savant’s Whiff%. The color scale no longer clips at 0.2.
  • K% and BB% use every completed plate appearance as the denominator. Intentional walks count as walks.
  • Several player IDs now return a named list of per-player plots. Previously the data was blended under the first player’s name.
  • Hard-hit rate excludes batted balls with no recorded exit velocity.
  • The hitter central-zone heat map now covers -1 to 1 ft horizontally. The (0.5, 1] column was previously dropped.
  • The general-stats tables add batters faced or plate appearances, pitcher whiff rate, pitch usage and hitter walk rate.

Other

  • Fixed the generate_pitcher() example ID for Gerrit Cole (543037).
  • Network examples are wrapped in \donttest{}.
  • Added an offline testthat suite with fixture data.
  • Removed unused dependencies: baseballr, dplyr, tidyr, kableExtra.
